I’m not convinced that the growth scare is warranted, or at least that it will be bad enough to change the direction of interest rates. If investors are worried about growth, why is breadth ample? Looking at the chart below, the tariff tantrum in the spring of last year was a proper growth scare and produced a 20% drawdown in the AI/ex-AI pair while breadth was very weak at 19%. Today we have a 22% drawdown and 61% breadth. Of course, the SPX is down only 3.4% today vs 21% last year April, but that distinction also tells me that this an AI-only scare and not a broader growth scare. 🧵(2/2)

The AI/ex-AI pair has now corrected 22% from its recent high, while simultaneously the 10-year Treasury yield is down 43 bps from its recent high of 5.36%. Coincidence? Probably not. The market seems to be betting on AI being systemic enough that a cresting or reversal of the capex boom will have broad implications on the economy and monetary policy. 🧵(1/2)

Measuring form the April 2025 low (which started the melt-up phase of this cycle) the cap-weighted and equal-weighted index are now even. The cap-weighted index has been “dead money” since the June 2 high, while underneath the surface things are churning. There are many examples of bull market cycles that took prolonged breaks without breaking sharply lower, and my guess is that we are in one of those phases. Think 1994, 2015, and 2018. All three years produced solid earnings growth which was offset by multiple compression.
